title: Fixed phrases
subtitle: out of the blue, so far, if I were you
summary: Learn groups of words that go together as one item - ring a bell, get rid of, now and again, to be honest.

lesson.heading: What are fixed phrases?
lesson.text: Some groups of words have to be learnt as complete phrases, because their meaning is different from the words on their own. Many of them are called **idioms**.

examples.note: I didn't know they were coming; it was unexpected.

examples.text: Does the name Merchant **ring a bell**?
You'll have to **make up your mind** soon.

lesson.heading: Easier fixed phrases
lesson.text: Other fixed phrases are easier to understand, but your own language may express the same idea in a different way.

examples.text: I think we'll have to **get rid of** some of this furniture.
examples.note: = sell it, throw it away, give it away

examples.text: I can't talk to you now; I'm just **about to** leave.
examples.note: = I am going to leave very soon

examples.text: Natalie **burst into tears**. She was very upset.

examples.note: = not including Yasmine; also except for

lesson.heading: Time phrases
rows: He's leaving in four days' time.
the week before the previous one
I got here the week before last.
The course is fine so far.
now, immediately (also right away, straight away)
She was able to come at once.
He comes home late night after night.

lesson.heading: Pairs of words
rows: first in one direction, then the other
I don't know when, but it will happen
lesson.note: A number of fixed phrases are two words joined by and, and sometimes or.

lesson.heading: Introducing advice, opinions and examples
lesson.text: Many fixed phrases introduce what you are going to say next.

examples.text: **If I were you**, I'd accept the job they offered you.
**In general** the summers are quite warm here.
examples.note: = usually, in most situations; also on the whole

examples.text: There were lots of questions. **For instance**, how much will it cost?
I'm sure you'll have a great holiday. **By the way**, what time does the train leave?
examples.note: used to introduce a new subject

examples.text: **To be honest**, I didn't like her boyfriend very much.
examples.note: used to say what you really think

lesson.heading: Six more useful idioms
rows: watch it and make sure it is safe
on the tip of my tongue
I know it but I can't remember it right now

lesson.text: Write a fixed phrase in your notebook as one whole item, with an example sentence - never word by word.

exercises.prompt: She's been working on that essay night ___ night.
exercises.explanation: Night after night means every night; we also say day after day.

exercises.prompt: My parents always turn up at my flat out of the ___.
exercises.explanation: Out of the blue means completely unexpectedly.

exercises.prompt: Match each fixed phrase with its meaning.
I'd like to get ___ of these CDs because I don't listen to them any more.
exercises.explanation: Get rid of something means remove it, sell it or throw it away.

exercises.prompt: Some people enjoyed the book, but ___, I thought it was boring.
exercises.explanation: To be honest introduces what you really think.

exercises.prompt: In ___, people are much happier when they have jobs that they enjoy.
exercises.explanation: In general means usually or on the whole.

exercises.prompt: I don't know what to do at the moment, but I'll have to make up my ___ soon.
exercises.explanation: Make up your mind means make a decision.

exercises.prompt: Is the missing word in these pairs and or or?
*A:* When are you going back? *B:* In two weeks' ___.
exercises.explanation: In two weeks' time means two weeks from now.

exercises.prompt: *A:* I spoke to Chris Myler. Do you know him? *B:* No, the name doesn't ring ___.
exercises.explanation: If a name rings a bell, it sounds familiar.

exercises.statement: If you say 'The course is fine so far', you mean it has been fine up until now.
exercises.explanation: Correct. So far means up until now.

exercises.prompt: Match these idioms with their meanings.

pairs.left: on the tip of my tongue
pairs.right: I know it but can't remember it now

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to give your friend some advice.
exercises.answer: If I were you, I'd accept the job they offered you.
exercises.explanation: If I were you introduces advice; it means 'in your situation'.
